[WHY]
For additional power savings
column2: PSR SU (also referred to as PSR2) can be

column1: enabled on eDP panels with PSR SU support.
PSR2 saves more power compared to PSR1 by allowing more opportunities
for the display hardware to be shut down. In comparison to PSR1
down can now occur in-between frames
column2: as well as in display regions

column1: where there is no visible update. In otherwords
display hw components to be enabled only for a **selectively updated**
region of the visible display. Hence PSR SU.
[HOW]
To define the SU region
column2: support from the OS is required. OS needs to

column1: inform driver of damaged regions that need to be flushed to the eDP
panel. Today
column2: such support is lacking in most compositors.

column1: Therefore
column2: an in-between solution is to implement PSR SU for MPO and

column1: cursor scenarios. The plane bounds can be used to define the damaged
region to be flushed to panel. This is achieved by:
* Leveraging dm_crtc_state->mpo_requested flag to identify when MPO is
enabled.
* If MPO is enabled
column2: only add updated plane bounds to dirty region.

column1: Determine plane update by either:
* Existence of drm damaged clips attached to the plane (added by a
damage-aware compositor)
* Change in fb id (flip)
* Change in plane bounds (position and dimensions)
* If cursor is enabled
column2: the old_pos and new_pos of cursor plus cursor

column1: size is used as damaged regions(*).
(*) Cursor updates follow a different code path through DC. PSR SU for
cursor is already implemented in DC
column2: and the only thing required to

column1: enable is to set DC_PSR_VERSION_SU_1 on the eDP link. See
